problem: Find the equation of the left-opening parabola that has its vertex at $(4,-3)$ and passes through the point $(1,0).$

feedback.problem: Find the equation of the left-opening parabola that has its vertex at $(-1,2)$ and passes through the point $(-2,6).$
feedback.worked_solution:
The general standard equation of a parabola whose vertex is $(h,k)$ and whose arms open right or left is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-k)^{2} & =4p(x-h).\end{aligned}
$$

Since we know that the given parabola has its vertex at $(h,k)=(-1,2),$ we substitute $h=-1$ and $k=2$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-2)^{2} & =4p(x+1).\end{aligned}
$$

We also know that the given parabola passes through the point $(-2,6),$ so we can substitute $x=-2$ and $y=6$ into the equation above and solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-2)^{2} & =4p(x+1) \\ (6-2)^{2} & =4p(-2+1) \\ 16 & =-4p \\ p & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation of the parabola is 

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-2)^{2} & =4p(x+1) \\ (y-2)^{2} & =4(-4)(x+1) \\ (y-2)^{2} & =-16(x+1).\end{aligned}
$$
